steps: Action potential depolarization is driven by opening of voltage-gated Na+ channels.
At the peak of the action potential, voltage-gated Na+ channels enter an inactivated state.
The absolute refractory period occurs because these Na+ channels cannot be reopened regardless of stimulus strength.
This inactivation state persists until the membrane potential repolarizes sufficiently.
Therefore, the primary cause of the absolute refractory period is the inactivation of voltage-gated Na+ channels.
